title: As and The More: Changes That Go Together

sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know *a medida que* and *cuanto más …, más …* from B1 Unit 2. *A medida que* + indicative describes a change in progress ("as"), and *cuanto más …, más …* says that the second change grows with the first ("the more …, the more …"); *cuanto menos* gives the opposite direction. An electric grid is a good case: demand, rain and power all move together.

items.spanish: A medida que crece el consumo de Paraguay, queda menos energía para vender a Brasil.
items.english: As Paraguay's consumption grows, less energy is left to sell to Brazil.

items.spanish: A medida que aumenta la demanda, las centrales producen más.
items.english: As demand increases, the power stations produce more.

items.spanish: Cuanto más se conectan las redes eléctricas, más fácil es compartir electricidad.
items.english: The more the electricity grids are connected, the easier it is to share electricity.

items.spanish: Cuanto menos llueve en la cuenca del Paraná, menos electricidad producen las centrales.
items.english: The less it rains in the Paraná basin, the less electricity the power stations produce.

sections.content: After *a medida que* use the indicative for a change that is really happening. *Cuanto* does not change when a verb follows it, and the second half starts with *más* or *menos*: *cuanto más estudio, más entiendo*.
